title: Has anyone tried using a state machine liked structure for LLM driven narratives?
author: ZeroOne11111
selftext: E.g. only feeding the current state + possible next states instead of the full story. And handling longer term memory separately.

comments.author: WhopperitoJr
comments.body: I have seen a few project-specific implementations. In terms of a plugin/tool, I have been working on this with [Personica AI](https://swamprabbitlabs.com/personica/) for Unreal Engine in an attempt to standardize and make it more accessible for developers. Especially if you are running local models like I am, a good RAG system/external reference is critical as you can't expect one LLM conversation to hold the memories for every character.

replies.author: ZeroOne11111
replies.body: I'm definitely using a RAG system for long-term memory. I'm current testing how well the LLM handles the details when combining a state machine (for logic) with story summaries (for context). Like each state to part of the story summary. Every time the detail varies a bit, not sure if it's good or not.

comments.author: Acceptable-Goose5144
comments.body:
It was definitely something that was needed. I’m building a similar structure for my own game as well, and I’ve already completed part of it. However, for now, I’m not planning to turn it into a commercial product in the short term.

I think the price of this product is good, but it shouldn’t be limited to Unreal only; other engines should be supported as well. It needs to be examined in detail.

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: You simply can't feed the full story for any game of decent length. I think most people (myself included) end up using summaries, state objects and RAG.  Counting on the LLM to remember everything is a losing battle.

comments.author: HrodRuck
comments.body:
I think this idea has potential. Like, letting the LLM pick or generate from a set of transistions and only having it treat the current state + future potential states as context. When it choses a future state, you swap to that and the cycle goes on. And you keep the state data not in a RAG or anything like that, but in a normal database that you feed the LLM as necessary.  


I'm doing something almost similar. Every state in my state machine would be a game level. The LLM only controls the current level, it doesn't need to worry about the ehole thing. For that, I used a dungeon-like structure, with specific points for entry and exit which are the other states in the machine (that can be adapted for a narrative).

  
tld;dr good idea

replies.author: ZeroOne11111
replies.body: I'm concerned about the detail drifting. As a player, small variations in details are nice surprises, but it’s a pain if you can’t replicate an outcome because the LLM changed a key detail. Or even worse no matter it changed, it guided to the same end.
